prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Story: HPE Networking Investor Day: $3B AI Orders, Synergy Raise & Analyst Targets. Related tickers: HPE, JNPR, AMD.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

Why this needs follow-up: HPE rose 7.36% on investor-day disclosures including $3B+ cumulative AI-networking orders, revised Juniper synergies to $800M, and a Vultr $1.2B order, but prior Juniper synergy target and multiple conflicting analyst price targets (Daiwa $75, Citi $92) are unreconciled in the notes.

ANSWER EACH QUESTION (run a separate search for each):
- What was HPE's prior Juniper Networks integration synergy target before it was raised to $800 million at the October 5 2026 Networking Investor Day?
- What price targets did Truist, Piper Sandler, Wells Fargo, and Evercore set for HPE following the October 2 2026 analyst events, and how do they compare to Daiwa's $75 and Citi's $92?
- Does the $1.2 billion Vultr Helios AI server order represent a new booking or a previously announced pipeline item, and what gross-margin profile did HPE indicate for Helios rack systems?

Name every stock affected by this story with its move, analyst notes that name winners and losers
(firm, rating, PT), exact figures (deal values, estimates, dates), and the latest status as of the
cutoff. Prefer Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC, WSJ, Barron's, MarketWatch, company releases, filings.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or sub-topic:

## TICKER or Sub-topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.

content:
## HPE [Juniper synergies and Investor Day]

- HPE raised its Juniper Networks acquisition annual run-rate cost-synergy target to **$800 million by the end of fiscal 2028**, from the previous target of **at least $600 million**; the increase was **$200 million**, or **33.3%** versus the prior minimum target. The Investor Day materials were published around **September 30–October 1, 2026**. (Economic Times, Oct. 4; Converge Digest, Oct. 1)
- HPE raised its fiscal 2027 Networking revenue-growth outlook to **high-teens to low-20s percentage growth**, from approximately **14%–17%** previously. (Telecompaper, Oct. 1)
- HPE said Networking operating margin should be in the **mid-to-high 20% range** from fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2029, compared with approximately **22%** in its recent fiscal third-quarter results. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 1; Business Insider, Oct. 2)
- HPE shares rose **7.36%** during the Friday, October 2, 2026 regular session following the networking disclosures. (User-provided brief; corroborating market coverage reported approximately 7.5%, MarketBeat, Oct. 2)
- HPE reported more than **$3 billion of cumulative AI-networking orders** at the Investor Day. (Story details supplied in the brief; no independently retrieved source with a publication timestamp was available in the search results.)
- HPE projected Data Center Networking revenue to grow at a **low-to-high 50s percentage compound annual rate through fiscal 2029**. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 1)

## HPE [Analyst actions and price targets]

- **Truist:** maintained **Buy** and raised its price target to **$75 from $70**. (MarketBeat, Oct. 2; Business Insider, Oct. 2)
- **Piper Sandler:** maintained **Neutral/Hold** and set a **$57** price target, down from **$63** in one October 2 market report. A separate report identified analyst James Fish as maintaining **Hold** with a **$70** target; the retrieved reports conflict on the current Piper Sandler target. (MarketBeat, Oct. 2; Business Insider, Oct. 1)
- **Wells Fargo:** maintained **Equal Weight/Hold** and raised its price target to **$63 from $54**. (MarketBeat, Oct. 2; Business Insider, Oct. 1)
- **Evercore:** no price target or rating was identified in the retrieved October 2–5 search results.
- **Daiwa Securities:** upgraded HPE to **Outperform from Neutral** and raised its price target to **$75 from $65**. (Business Insider, Oct. 2)
- **Citigroup:** maintained **Buy** and raised its price target to **$92 from $76**. (MarketBeat, Oct. 2; Business Insider, Oct. 1)
- Citi’s **$92** target was **$17 above** the **$75** targets from Daiwa and Truist, while Wells Fargo’s **$63** target was **$12 below** them; Piper Sandler’s reported targets were **$57** and **$70** in conflicting reports. (MarketBeat, Oct. 2; Business Insider, Oct. 1–2)
- **Susquehanna:** maintained **Neutral** and raised its price target to **$70 from $40**, citing the Networking Investor Day and the **$1.2 billion** Helios order. (Markets Insider, Oct. 2)
- **UBS:** maintained **Neutral** and raised its price target to **$66 from $59**. (MarketBeat, Oct. 2)
- **Morgan Stanley:** maintained **Overweight** and raised its price target to **$72 from $67**. (Business Insider, Oct. 2)
- **Barclays:** maintained **Overweight** and raised its price target to **$83 from $79**. (Business Insider, Oct. 1)
- The retrieved reports gave no confirmed October 2–5 **Evercore** rating or price target, so no Evercore figure is included.

## HPE / AMD [Vultr Helios order]

- Vultr placed a **$1.2 billion order** with HPE for **AMD Helios AI Rack systems** for deployment at Vultr’s U.S. data centers. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 1)
- HPE described the Vultr transaction as the **first purchase of the AMD Helios architecture**, indicating a **new booking rather than a previously announced pipeline item**. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 1)
- Each Helios rack integrates **72 AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs**, AMD EPYC “Venice” CPUs, AMD Pensando Vulcano AI-networking chips, AMD ROCm software, and **six HPE Juniper Networking QFX5252 scale-up Ethernet switch trays**. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 1)
- HPE said the Vultr order built on nearly **three years of collaboration** between Vultr and Juniper Networks, but the reported **$1.2 billion** was identified as the first purchase of the new Helios system. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 1)
- HPE indicated a **mid-to-high 20% operating-margin range** for the Networking segment, but the retrieved sources did not provide a separate **gross-margin percentage specifically for Helios rack systems**. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 1)
- HPE reported company non-GAAP gross margin of **40.4%**, approximately **1,050 basis points higher year over year**, but that figure was not identified as the Helios rack-system gross margin. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 1)

## AMD [Helios exposure]

- AMD was named as the processor and accelerator supplier in HPE’s **$1.2 billion Vultr Helios order**; the system uses **72 AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs per rack**, AMD EPYC “Venice” CPUs, AMD Pensando Vulcano networking chips, and AMD ROCm software. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 1)
- The retrieved search results did not provide a timestamped October 2–5 regular-session, after-hours, overnight, or pre-market percentage move for **AMD** attributable to the HPE announcement.

## JNPR [Juniper integration]

- HPE’s Juniper integration target increased from **at least $600 million** to **$800 million** in annual run-rate savings by fiscal 2028. (Economic Times, Oct. 4)
- Juniper Networks was acquired by HPE in **July 2025** and operates inside HPE after the transaction; the synergy figure is therefore an **HPE integration target**, not standalone Juniper guidance. (Economic Times, Oct. 4; Ad-hoc News, Oct. 4)
- The retrieved search results did not provide a separate October 2–5 stock-price move for **JNPR**; Juniper had been acquired by HPE and was no longer presented as an independently traded operating company in the cited coverage. (Ad-hoc News, Oct. 4)
